optimize_reason: Dual-horizon cash-return-on-assets: the annual trend plus the most recent quarterly change in the same quantity. Cash flow on assets already cleared every hard threshold (Sharpe 1.64, Fitness 1.03, two-year 1.97) but sits right at the 5.01% turnover floor; adding the fast leg of the same economic quantity raises turnover with margin while confirming the annual trend is still accelerating rather than decaying.

Dual-horizon asset-turnover trend. Asset turnover produced the best two-year Sharpe (2.44) and best sub-universe Sharpe (1.41) of the whole campaign because revenue over assets carries almost no cross-jurisdictional accounting-policy content; its only gap is turnover at 4.34%. Adding the quarterly leg lifts turnover while preserving the policy-free nature of the signal.

EBITDA on assets with the widest market-wide benchmark. EBITDA removes depreciation and amortisation policy, which differs systematically between regions and is the main reason earnings-based measures behave inconsistently across AMER, EMEA and APAC; the market-wide benchmark additionally maximizes dispersion.

Dual-horizon EBIT-on-assets trend benchmarked market-wide. Combines the two strongest levers found so far - the asset denominator that removes the pro-cyclical self-damping of revenue, and the market-wide benchmark that maximizes retained dispersion - while the quarterly leg pushes turnover clear of the floor.
